license_note: Every dimension row is derived from openrocket/openrocket-database (Apache-2.0; Dave Cook et al., 2014-2022), files estes_classic.orc, loc_precision.orc, madcow.orc, bluetube.orc, publicmissiles.orc, giantleaprocketry.orc (+ estes_ps2.orc and generic_materials.orc for the supplement), via parse-orc.mjs and curate-airframes.mjs. The numbers are vendor catalogue facts (LOC Precision, Madcow Rocketry, Always Ready Rocketry, Public Missiles Ltd, Giant Leap Rocketry, Estes) hand-transcribed by volunteers; the .orc files carry explicit SOURCE ERROR and "assumed" comments that this table cites per row. Skeptic-supplied numbers (supplement, disputed) are recall unless a source line is cited. thrustcurve-db (broofa, ISC; John Coker ThrustCurve.org) is NOT used in this table.

columns.key: unique row id: <kind abbr>_<vendor>_<first PN slug>
columns.kind: BodyTube | TubeCoupler | CenteringRing, exactly as the curated/upstream file classed it (see part_role for what it really is)
columns.part_role: derived from the upstream Description: airframe, motor_mount_tube, switch_band, piston, coupler, coupler_stiffener, centering_ring, coupler_ring
columns.vendor: Estes | LOC | Madcow | Blue Tube (ARR) | PML | Giant Leap
columns.material: curated material class (note: Madcow 'G12 fiberglass' rings are really G10 sheet; Giant Leap MAG/DY rows are Magnaframe/Dynawind - see material_raw and disputed)
columns.material_raw: the upstream .orc material string(s) for the grouped parts
columns.family: cross-vendor airframe class the part belongs to (tubes: by ID; couplers and rings: by OD = the airframe ID they ride in)
columns.mmt_class: CenteringRing only: motor-tube class the ring ID is nearest (18/24/29/38/54/75/98 mm); it does NOT guarantee the ring clears every vendor tube of that class - see disputed
columns.id_mm: inside diameter, mm (BodyTube/TubeCoupler: bore; CenteringRing: the motor-tube OD it is meant to slide over)
columns.od_mm: outside diameter, mm (BodyTube: airframe OD; TubeCoupler: the airframe ID it enters; CenteringRing: the airframe ID it sits in)
columns.wall_mm: (od_mm - id_mm)/2: tube wall for BodyTube/TubeCoupler; RADIAL WEB WIDTH for CenteringRing (duplicated as web_mm)
columns.id_in: id_mm / 25.4 to 3 dp (recovers the vendor inch figure when inch_exact is true)
columns.inch_exact: true when both mm values are exact 3-dp inch conversions (i.e. the upstream entry was in inches); false = upstream entered mm (26 Giant Leap rows), the inch value shown is a back-conversion
columns.nominal: vendor's own size string, heterogeneous (inch sizes, mm sizes, Madcow FT codes such as '60' = 6.0 in, CR pair codes such as '5429' = 54 mm airframe / 29 mm MMT, Estes BT names); NOT a lookup key
columns.pns: up to 4 part numbers grouped in this row; pns_all lists all when more were grouped
columns.lengths_mm: up to 6 stock lengths, mm (for CenteringRing this is the ring THICKNESS, duplicated as thickness_mm); lengths_all_mm lists all when more were grouped
columns.thickness_mm: CenteringRing only: ring thickness values, mm (2.337 = 0.092 in G10, 3.175 = 1/8 in, 4.762 = 3/16 in, 6.35 = 1/4 in, 12.7 = 1/2 in)
columns.web_mm: CenteringRing only: radial web (od_mm - id_mm)/2, mm
columns.upstream_desc: the upstream Description text (first, or up to 6 when grouped) - the only place the source says piston / stiffener / coupler-ring / switch band
columns.cross_check: present where a skeptic's independent recall matched the tabled value
columns.disputed: list of {field, table_value, skeptic_value, skeptic_confidence, source, verified_upstream?, note?}: the table value is KEPT; this records what a reviewer believes instead and why
columns.confidence: certain | likely | recall - applies to id_mm/od_mm as vendor NOMINALS. Nothing in this table is 'certain': all values are volunteer transcriptions of vendor catalogue pages
columns.source: upstream .orc file and its provenance comments

notes: READ BEFORE CUTTING. (1) Every id/od here is a catalogue NOMINAL transcribed by volunteers, not a measurement; coupler/tube and ring/tube pairs in this data have zero or negative clearance (all PML CT-x, GL C-2.56, LOC TC-1.52, GL rings), which proves it. No fit may be machined from a table value alone: mic the actual tube at three clockings, size to the measured diameter with a stated diametral clearance, and cut a test ring before the final part. Treat FG ID as +/-0.13 mm, FG OD +/-0.25 mm, kraft/phenolic +/-0.25 mm and out-of-round (recall). (2) KNOWN BAD ROWS (kept, flagged in 'disputed'): PML QT-2.5 ID 54.661 (should be ~65.024); GL B-3.00 OD 77.851 / wall 0.8 mm; GL C-7.512-L length 30.968 (48 in); GL 'MAG 6.0 x 48, PH 7.5 x 48' nominal 6.0 (it is a 7.5 in tube); Madcow FCR8075 merged with FCR8098 dims; Blue Tube CR-54/29 OD 57.633 (~54.483); LOC CR-1.52-18mm ID 18.771 (< MMT OD 19.431) and LOC CR-1.52-* OD 38.659 (> BT-1.52 ID 38.608); Madcow FT80 ID 198.12 vs 198.501; Madcow FT115 (assumed by upstream); Madcow CR3954 ID 57.099 (< T54 OD). Seven PML PS-x rows are pistons, six LOC STC-x rows are coupler stiffeners, LOC CRTC-* and Madcow FCR39C54 are coupler-fit rings: filter on part_role, not kind. All 29 Madcow 'G12' rings are G10 sheet. (3) CONFIDENCE POLICY: LOC and Giant Leap rows are 'recall' (LOC file header: LOC never published good size data; GL is a legacy Rocksim file, mostly discontinued); LOC, Blue Tube and Giant Leap centering rings are synthesized from tube sizes by the database author; Madcow G12/plywood/G10, Blue Tube tubes/couplers, PML phenolic and Estes BT are 'likely' (independently matched by three skeptics' recall and by the upstream master on raw.githubusercontent.com); Madcow carbon (copies of G12), Madcow kraft couplers (dims missing upstream), PML glassed phenolic and the disputed rows are 'recall'. Nothing is 'certain'. (4) DOCTRINE for 'N inch airframe' with no vendor: never resolve to a single number silently. Return the candidate rows across vendors/materials (with vendor, PN, ID/OD, confidence) and ask for vendor + material, offering the families by name. If the user insists: 3 in -> ID 3.000 in (76.200 mm; PML 3.002), OD UNKNOWN in 3.098-3.126 in; 4 in -> ID 3.900 in (99.060 mm; Estes BT-101 3.896), OD 4.000 (LOC) vs 4.024 (Madcow/Blue Tube/PML); 6 in -> assume ID 6.000 in / 152.400 mm (modal: Madcow, Wildman, Blue Tube, Giant Leap; PML/legacy GL 6.007 / 152.578; LOC recall 6.00/6.16) and treat OD as UNKNOWN in the 6.125-6.20 in (155.6-157.5 mm) band; 7.5 in -> ID 7.500-7.518 in across vendors (couplers/bulkheads NOT interchangeable), OD 7.660-7.708; 5.5 in is AMBIGUOUS (ID 5.375 Madcow FT55 / 5.38 LOC vs 5.500 Blue Tube, 3.2 mm apart) and must be asked, never assumed; 8 in -> ID 7.800 or 7.815 per the source conflict. If only 'fiberglass' is given, default to the Madcow/Wildman row, say so explicitly, and mark the answer 'assumed vendor'. (5) Which surface matters: parts that ride on the airframe ID (internal bulkheads, centering-ring OD, nose-cone shoulders) may be designed to the family ID plus a documented clearance with a 'measure to confirm' note. Parts that engage the OD (retainer flanges, fin cans, tailcones, boattails, rail-button standoffs, external sleeves) or the coupler ID (av-bay end caps, sled rails) MUST have vendor + material or, better, a caliper measurement, because OD spread within a family exceeds 1 mm and coupler-ID spread in the 6 in class is 2.1 mm (Madcow FC60 146.685 / Blue Tube 148.565 / PML 148.819). When neither is available, emit the part parametrically with the fit diameter as a named variable and refuse to emit a press-fit dimension. (6) Motor-tube ODs for retainer bores are vendor-specific: 29 mm = 30.734 LOC / 30.861 Madcow paper / 31.877 Madcow G12 / 32.131 GL / 32.233 PML / 32.36 Blue Tube; 38 mm = 40.64-41.91; 54 mm = 56.642-57.861; 75 mm = 78.689-79.4 (LOC MMTHD 79.248); 98 mm = 101.6-102.362 (LOC MMTHD 102.108). LOC 75/98 mm rings were synthesized around the thin BT-3.00/BT-3.9, not the MMTHD tubes. (7) Every generated fit for a tube-mating part must carry a caliper-measured override field and a test-ring step before final cut. Print the row (vendor, PN, ID/OD, confidence) used.
